podcast.title: Breakthrough Album
podcast.body: Lana Del Rey broke through in 2012 with this album after several years out of the spotlight. It was characterized by a noir and femme-fatale aesthetic, with storytelling and moodiness that evoked various subtle emotions, exemplifying the whisper pop style. "It was all very noir and rather femme-fatale with its storytelling and moodiness, evocative of many different subtle emotions."

podcast.title: Debut Album
podcast.body: This album achieved significant commercial success, reaching gold status and then platinum, and hitting number 1 in many countries. It is widely included in lists of the best albums of the decade and is noted for having six distinct singles that entered the sales charts, a feat shared only with Lady Gaga in the same century. Critics were divided, with some hailing it as a masterpiece and others in the UK calling it a "completely pre-fabricated and mediated album by a record label." The album's themes were extensively reworked with Justin Parker to be more aesthetic, with Lana Del Rey herself stating it's based on a "trilogy of three places" she lived: New York (adolescence), London (symphonic and baroque music influences), and Miami (retro 50s aesthetic). Its cover art and subsequent album covers (Ultraviolence, Honeymoon) were photographed in or around Miami. "Ella hizo un disco que fue disco de oro, después se cooperquía en disco del platinho, fue número 1, un montón de países, y hoy en día, esta incluiden, prácticamente todas las listas de el mejor disco de la década."

podcast.title: Thematic Interpretation
podcast.body: In an interview, Lana Del Rey claimed that the "Born to Die" album was about the "first great love of her life," which she identified as alcohol. This interpretation highlights a theme she introduced, though the album's themes were heavily influenced and rewritten with Justin Parker. "ella llegó a decir que el morto está y trata del primer gran amor de su vida, que fue la alcohol, fijaros, esa es el mundo, ya llegaba con estas temas."

podcast.title: Top 10 Vinyl Seller of 2010s
podcast.body: Lana Del Rey's 2012 album "Born to Die" made it into the top 10 best-selling vinyl records of the 2010s. This achievement is notable as it was a contemporary release performing strongly in a resurgent retro format. "Its Lannadell race born to die in 2012. These vinyl sales went up."
